verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's docs clearly state that flags can be enabled or disabled independently per environment (dev, staging, production). Rules can be scoped to environments, and a toggle endpoint switches flags in specific environments. SDK connections exist and serve a read-only subset of flag data, but no evidence ties an SDK key to a single environment, and custom environments sit on a higher pricing tier. missing for 10: explicit documentation that SDK keys/connections are scoped per environment, independent or hands-on corroboration of environment isolation, clarity on which environments are available below the custom-environments tier.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage separate environments (dev/staging/prod) with independent flag states and scoped SDK keys

citations.quote: Use environments such as dev, staging, and production to enable or disable feature flags independently.
Feature flags can be enabled and disabled on a per-environment basis.
the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
The SDK Connection Endpoint provides readonly access to a subset of your feature flag data, just enough for the GrowthBook SDKs to assign values to users.
